provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Revision of Surah Al-Fatihah
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite Surah Al-Fatihah.
The pupils should be able to state the short meaning of Surah Al-Fatihah.

Introduction:
We have learned Surah Al-Fatihah before. Today we will revise it together.

Content:
Surah Al-Fatihah is the first surah of the Quran. It has seven verses. We recite it in every prayer. The short meaning is: Praise be to Allah, Lord of all worlds.

Class activity:
The teacher will lead the class in reciting Surah Al-Fatihah together.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is the first surah of the Quran?
2. How many verses are in Surah Al-Fatihah?
3. Why do we recite Surah Al-Fatihah?

Summary:
Surah Al-Fatihah is very important and we must know it well.

topics.title: Surah Al-Fil
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tell the story of the elephant.
The pupils should be able to explain how Allah protects His house.

Introduction:
Last week we revised Surah Al-Fatihah. Today we learn about Surah Al-Fil.

Content:
Surah Al-Fil tells about Abrahah who wanted to destroy Kaaba. He came with many elephants. But Allah sent birds that threw stones at them. The elephants ran away. Allah protects His house.

Class activity:
The teacher will tell the story with actions and pupils will repeat.

Evaluation questions:
1. What animal did Abrahah use?
2. How did Allah protect the Kaaba?
3. What do we learn from this surah?

Summary:
Allah is strong and He protects His house.

topics.title: Surah Al-Quraysh
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list the trade journeys of Quraysh.
The pupils should be able to explain how Allah provides for us.

Introduction:
We learned about Surah Al-Fil last week. Today we will learn Surah Al-Quraysh.

Content:
Surah Al-Quraysh tells about how Quraysh traveled to Yemen for trade in summer and to Sham for trade in winter. Allah made them safe on these journeys. Allah provides for us through our work.

Class activity:
Pupils will act out traveling to market for trade like the Quraysh.

Evaluation questions:
1. Where did Quraysh travel in summer?
2. Where did they travel in winter?
3. How does Allah provide for us?

Summary:
Allah helps us in our work and travel.

topics.title: The Prophet's birth
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify Makkah as the Prophet's birthplace.
The pupils should be able to explain why we love the Prophet (SAW).

Introduction:
Last week we learned about Surah Al-Quraysh. Today we learn about the Prophet's birth.

Content:
The Prophet Muhammad (SAW) was born in Makkah. His father died before he was born. His grandfather and uncle took care of him. We love the Prophet because he taught us good things.

Class activity:
Pupils will draw a simple map of Makkah with the Kaaba.

Evaluation questions:
1. Where was the Prophet born?
2. Who took care of the Prophet after his father died?
3. Why do we love the Prophet?

Summary:
The Prophet was born in Makkah and we love him very much.

topics.title: The Prophet's honesty
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain why the Prophet was called Al-Amin.
The pupils should be able to give examples of being truthful.

Introduction:
We learned about the Prophet's birth last week. Today we learn about his honesty.

Content:
The Prophet was called Al-Amin which means the truthful. Even before he became a prophet, people trusted him with their things. When he was young, he worked for Khadija and gave back all the money. We must be truthful like the Prophet.

Class activity:
Pupils will role-play situations where they can be truthful.

Evaluation questions:
1. What does Al-Amin mean?
2. Give an example of the Prophet's honesty.
3. How can we be truthful like the Prophet?

Summary:
The Prophet was always truthful and we should be too.

topics.title: Salat: the positions
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate ruku and sujud.
The pupils should be able to explain why we pray with care.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about the Prophet's honesty. Today we learn about salat positions.

Content:
In salat, we have many positions. Ruku is when we bend our back and praise Allah. Sujud is when we put our head down on the floor and ask for forgiveness. We pray with care because it is talking to Allah.

Class activity:
The teacher will demonstrate ruku and sujud and pupils will follow.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is ruku?
2. What is sujud?
3. Why should we pray with care?

Summary:
We must know all positions in salat and pray well.

topics.title: Du'a for knowledge
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite the du'a for knowledge.
The pupils should be able to explain why we pray before study.

Introduction:
We learned about salat positions last week. Today we learn about du'a for knowledge.

Content:
We should pray before we study. We say: Allah, increase my knowledge. The Prophet taught us to ask Allah for knowledge. When we pray, Allah helps us understand better.

Class activity:
Pupils will practice saying the du'a for knowledge together.

Evaluation questions:
1. What do we say before studying?
2. Why should we pray before study?
3. What did the Prophet teach us about knowledge?

Summary:
We must always pray to Allah for knowledge.

topics.title: Allah the Creator
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify signs of Allah in nature.
The pupils should be able to say Subhanallah when seeing beautiful things.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about du'a for knowledge. Today we learn about Allah the Creator.

Content:
Allah created everything. We see His signs in nature - the sun, trees, and animals. When we see something beautiful, we say Subhanallah which means Allah is free from all defects.

Class activity:
The teacher will show pictures of nature and pupils will say Subhanallah.

Evaluation questions:
1. Who created everything?
2. Name two signs of Allah in nature.
3. What do we say when we see something beautiful?

Summary:
Allah is the Creator of all things.

topics.title: Kindness to neighbours
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tell the Prophet's teaching about neighbours.
The pupils should be able to give examples of being a good neighbour.

Introduction:
We learned about Allah the Creator last week. Today we learn about kindness to neighbours.

Content:
The Prophet said that Jibril kept telling him to be kind to neighbours. A good neighbour helps others, shares food, and speaks nicely. We should treat our neighbours like family.

Class activity:
Pupils will make cards for their neighbours to show kindness.

Evaluation questions:
1. What did the Prophet teach about neighbours?
2. Give one way to be a good neighbour.
3. Why is it important to be kind to neighbours?

Summary:
We must be kind to our neighbours always.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall what they learned this term.
The pupils should be able to recite the surahs they learned.

Introduction:
Today we will revise all we learned this term and have a small test.

Content:
We learned about Surah Al-Fatihah, Al-Fil, Al-Quraysh, the Prophet's life, salat, du'a, Allah the Creator, and kindness to neighbours. We must remember all these things.

Class activity:
The teacher will ask questions about all topics and pupils will answer.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name one surah we learned this term.
2. What is one thing we learned about the Prophet?
3. How should we treat our neighbours?
4. What is ruku in salat?

Summary:
We must remember all we learned about Islam and practice it.
